title: A Good Drying Day, Explained
subtitle: Ylva Ogunbanjo on why the basket, not the forecast, puts the washing out, and what brings it in when the rain arrives
summary: A research explainer from the School of Emergent Priorities on Ylva Ogunbanjo's doctoral thesis about the backyard washing line under a doubtful sky. It walks one morning's load from the full basket to the first drops, setting a two-year census of 312 lines and twelve weeks of household diaries beside the forecast every household could read. The School's Armful Rule is read in full at the end, and Ogunbanjo describes the census and the argument herself.
topic: A research explainer of the doctoral thesis on how households decide to peg the washing out under a doubtful sky, from a two-year census of 312 backyard lines, twelve weeks of load-by-load diaries and the timed dash to bring the washing in when rain begins, finding that the basket decides, the forecast is consulted afterwards and a load within one armful is what keeps the washing dry, and closing on the School's Armful Rule
